curated_by: attended session (Claude Code), agent-reach build slice
note: Curated official resolution-source URLs per market, plus the event triggers that
decide which of them are worth fetching on a given day. This is the 'honest bulk
of the work' the scoping note called for, and it is DATA, not code: adding a
source is a JSON edit plus a probe record, never a code change.
Every entry was probed live through the Jina path on the `curated` date and
carries what came back in `probe`. The load-bearing field is
probe.published_time, because the APPROVED timestamp rule dates a Jina item by
the `Published Time:` header and DISCARDS the item when that header is absent:
verified  - the header is present and equals the document's release instant.
touch     - the header is present but is an edit time on a rolling page. Such
a page can only ever be an `index` (navigation), never an item.
absent    - no header at all. The origin sends no Last-Modified (most modern
CDN-fronted government sites) or sends a stale/meaningless one.
fetch_clock - a stamp that tracks the FETCH instant, so it is always 'now'.
Discovered during this build and the most dangerous class: it is
never after the cutoff, so the approved after-cutoff check cannot
catch it, and it back-dates nothing — a month-old document enters
as today's news. centcom.mil and nobelprize.org both do this.
blocked   - r.jina.ai could not reach it at all (403/404).
MEASURED 2026-08-24: of 22 probed web sources, exactly ONE (federalreserve.gov
dated press releases) returns a usable publication timestamp. Sources measured
`absent` or `blocked` ship with enabled=false so they do not burn fetches on a
gate rejection that is already known — they stay here as curated provenance and
flip on the day either the site starts serving a timestamp or Justin approves an
additional declared timestamp source. The YouTube path is unaffected: yt-dlp
carries real upload timestamps everywhere, so the transcript channel is the one
that generalises.
roles:  document = an immutable dated document, ingestable as an evidence item.
index    = a rolling page. NAVIGATION ONLY. Fetched so the attended
agent can find today's dated document; never an item itself.
When it declares a `child` block, documents discovered under
it may be submitted and are pinned to that url_prefix.
video    = a transcript job. With `channel` and no `video_id` it is a
discovery job: submit the matching video as a child.
triggers: always | weekday {weekdays} | window {start,end} |
calendar {calendar, offsets_days}
